library(tidyverse)

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
hispanicpop <-get_acs(geography= 'state', table= 'B03003', year=2023, survey='acs5')
orderhispanicpop <- hispanicpop %>% filter(variable == 'B03003_003') %>% select(NAME, estimate) %>% arrange(desc(estimate))

orderhispanicpop

#code ran to determine which states had largest hispanic population to narrow down as whole country was too broad
#selected states: California, Texas, New York (1 from each coast)
#Note: having year=2023 with survey=acs5 means data is being pulled from 2018-2023
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#keeps selected states 
states <- c('California', 'Texas', 'New York')

#pulls education attainment then sorts by states I selected above 
hedu <- get_acs(geography = 'state', table = 'B15003I', year = 2023, survey = 'acs5')

stateedu <- hedu %>% filter(NAME %in% states) %>% mutate(category = case_when(variable %in% c('B15003I_022', 'B15003I_023', 'B15003I_024', 'B15003I_025') ~ 'College', variable != 'B15003I_001' ~ 'NCollege', TRUE ~ 'Total')) %>% 
  filter(category != 'Total') %>% group_by(NAME, category) %>% summarize(population = sum(estimate), .groups = 'drop') %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = population) %>% mutate(total = College + NCollege, percollege = College / total, perncollege = NCollege / total)

#pulls a median income 
hispincome <- get_acs(geography = 'state', table = 'B19013I', year = 2023, survey = 'acs5') %>% filter(NAME %in% states) %>% select(NAME, median_income = estimate)

#going to use get_pums to be able to better compare;right now the analysis is ecological
pumsdat <- get_pums(variables = c('AGEP', 'HISP', 'EDUC', 'PINCP'), state = c('CA','TX','NY'), year = 2023, survey = 'acs5')
  

#joining education and income to compare
edu_inc <- hedu %>% left_join(hispincome, by = NAME) %>% arrange(desc(percollege))
edu_inc

#Note: All data is pulled from; all codes (B15003I) are how things are coded in tidycensus; left join was used because edu is the main dataset, also accounts for any missing data in income 
#STILL NEED: make sure median outcome is also filtered by college and no college; can't do this, figuring out another way 
```
